- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., +5%+ from 18-day mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.2), model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast mean for 5–7 day horizon.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5–7 forecast days.
- If 18-day history shows strong upward trend, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast slope after day 10–12.
- When sentiment history shows no clear direction (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance; use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.
